claims.claim: A new model shows that gas falling onto early supermassive black holes from random directions keeps their spin low, shortening the growth timescale from 45 million years to roughly 27–32 million years.
claims.episode_span: A new model shows that gas falling onto early supermassive black holes from random directions keeps their spin low.
claims.source_title: Early black holes may have grown through productive chaos
claims.supporting_quote: The 'chaos' in our model comes from how gas reaches the black hole. We consider a slowly rotating dark matter halo, so that gas falls in from essentially random directions.
